full_judgment:
2. The facts, in brief, are that the petitioner is a registered Private Company and it carries on business of transport specially cargo and passenger marine vessel. The Company has registered office at 59 Dilkusha Commercial Area Dhaka. The respondent Bank sanctioned loan of Taka 22 lac in favour of the petitioner company on 2-2-1979 for construction of passenger Marine vessel of two engines and in terms of the sanction petitioner company executed necessary loan agreement and registered document of mortgage at the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies as documents of security of the vessel MV Kadam Rasul against the loan vide Annexure 'A' and 'B' respectively. Thereafter the petitioner company, the respondent Bank and construction company named Messer’s Progoti Ship Builder and Engineering Works Limited entered into a tripartite agreement amongst them on 12-7-1980 for construction of the vessel and in terms of the agreement the petitioner company would deposit its equity money in the respondent Bank and the respondent Bank would provide the loan facility. It was agreed that the respondent Bank would make all the payments to ship builder company directly and first payment would be made after completion of 40% of the works. The said tripartite agreement has been annexed and marked as Annexure 'C' ; that due to lapses of the Bank and the dockyard company the fate of the project became frustrated and the petitioner company was indebted to take step for completion of the half done work and, as such, had to invest additional equity money as well as take additional loan of Taka 15 lac. As a result the petitioner incurred substantial loss; in spite of adverse situation the petitioner succeeded to complete project and went into commercial service and started repayment of loan. The respondent Bank in violation of terms and conditions of the loan filed certificate case hearing No. 21-BSB/86 on 30-6-1986 before the General Certificate Officer, Dhaka and the petitioner was ordered to pay Taka 56,74,232 within 30 days. The petitioner filed the suit being TS No. 4 of 1989 before the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2 Dhaka for declaration that the claim of the respondent Bank as included in the certificate proceeding was not due to the Bank and total amount recoverable from the certificate debtor as on 30-6-1986 was Taka 11,14,920.90. The said suit was dismissed on contest; that against the impugned judgment and decree passed in the aforesaid suit the petitioner company preferred Appeal being First Appeal No. 57 of 1989 before the High Court Division and on 30-8-1989 further proceeding of the said certificate case No. 21-BSB/86 was stayed in Civil Rule No. 88 (1)89 subject to deposit of Taka 5 lac to the respondent Bank within 6(six) months and the petitioner company having made the deposit within stipulated time on 18-2-1990 the Rule was made absolute. During pendency of the First Appeal before the High Court Division an application was filed stating that the certificate proceeding initiated against the petitioner has been cancelled. As a result of cancellation of the proceeding no cause of action for the suit subsisted and the aforesaid appeal also became infructuous. The High Court Division being satisfied with the order of cancellation of the certificate proceeding passed order dated 22-5-1991 dismissing the appeal as being infructuous vide annexure 'D'. 

 3. The Borrower Company filed TS No. 180/1991 in the Third Court of the Subordinate Judge for declaration and also filed Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1989 which are still pending. The respondent Bank by letter No. 7-1324(AA) offered the Company opportunity to adjust/regularize the loan and in response the company deposited sum of Taka 5, 86.000 on 29-12-1991. Thereafter the Bank published sale notice in the Daily Star dated 14th May 1999 inviting Tender for sale of the vessel MV Kadam Rasul owned by the petitioner company under Article 34 of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank Order (President's Order No. 129 of 1972) 

 9. The ground Nos.1-3 taken by Writ petitioner are that the claim is barred by limitation, no notice under rule 3 of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank (Direct Sale of Mortgaged Property) Rules, 1980 having been served, the impugned notice is without lawful authority and that the respondent bank having realised Taka 5 lac and then having withdrawn the case it would be deemed that the Bank has withdrawn that claim and, as such, there is no liability now according to law laid down in Order 2 rule 2 CPC. 

 10. Dr M Zahir, the learned Advocate, has not pointed out to any specific provision of law in support of his contention to show that the claim is barred by limitation. The petitioner company is industrial concern which is under liability to the Bank under an agreement and deed of mortgage to repay the arrear dues to the Bank. The claim of the Bank cannot be said to be barred by limitation. There is nothing on record to show that BSB ever relinquished its claim fully or in part in favour of the petitioner so order 2 rule 2 has no manner of application in this case. We find no substance in ground Nos. 1 and 3 of the Writ petition. 

 (1) The bidder or tenderer whose bid or-tender is accepted shall have to deposit, within seven days of the said acceptance half of the bid or tender money in any branch of the Bank and in default of such deposit the hid or tender shall stand rejected and the earnest money deposited with the bid or tender, as the case may be shall stand forfeited to the Bank. 

 (2) If the bidder or tenderer has made the deposit as required under sub-rule (1) he shall deposit the balance amount within thirty days from the date of auction or acceptance of the tender, as the case may be and, in default of such deposit the half of the bid money or tender money deposited under sub-rule (1) shall stand forfeited to the Bank and the mortgaged property may be resold". 

 19. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and our findings above we find no substance in the contention of Mr Huda the learned Advocate.
